steps.content: [Guerrilla Tent]

steps.speaker: Helena
steps.content: Brock, is your brain even connected to your mouth?! Or did that sandstorm just swallow all your promises the second you stepped outside?! This is the 182nd time! THE 182ND TIME you've broken your word!!!

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Eeeek!!

steps.speaker: Helena
steps.content: "The modified Hypercube barriers are for protection, not for offense!" How was that not clear?! I said avoid the enemies, not go hunting them down while wearing the barriers in broad daylight!

steps.speaker: Helena
steps.content: I only snuck those notes to my boss and smuggled the supplies because you swore you'd play it safe! And this is how you repay me??!!

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I promise I won't get you in trouble, okay?

steps.speaker: Helena
steps.content: This isn't about getting me in trouble! EDGE is a scientific organization that belongs to all of humanity! We oppose war!! I want peace. Actual PEACE! Do you even know how to spell that word? Does "keeping your promise" mean anything to you at all?!

steps.speaker: Helena
steps.content: It's because you always pull this crap that I—

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: I'm wrong, I'm a jerk, I'm the worst! I'll kneel on nails next time—ah, crud, someone's here, gotta bounce, talk later!
[Clack—]

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Sigh... I finally get to call her, and all she does is yell at me?
A little head popped into view. It was Catherine.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Your wife?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You've dealt some real damage to our commander. The Andohar family would be proud of you.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Oh... She dumped you?

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: She's a comrade. Period! We watch each other's backs, not go on dinner dates. What kind of mushy stuff are you kids reading anyway?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Hmm... She's from Nirvana Port, then? Why would the guerrillas have ties to DisCity's industrial port? What has she been shipping to you?

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: ...Where did you hear that?
A small combat knife pressed against Catherine's throat, and the joyful atmosphere immediately shattered.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: That's a bold approach to intelligence gathering. You know, spies are executed here.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: For real?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Then, can you use a gun instead? Bullets are faster. Blocking them would be more exciting.
As requested, DisCity Major Dravyn drew his gun and chambered a round.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Whoa, whoa, hold up! She's just a kid, no need for all that. And you, kiddo, quit snooping around—and messing with our ammo. We're on a budget here!

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: You took a wrong turn and ended up in our backyard, it happens! We'll get you sorted and back home, alright?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: If you're worried about a "diplomatic incident," keeping me here seems like the safer choice, doesn't it? Things might get boring if I leave.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Why should we keep you here?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Because you need to keep secrets.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: You see, I know a few. The DisCity army was ordered by the metropoles to eliminate Captain Brock for his little rebellion. And yet, here you are—their military rising star—in his camp instead of leading the charge against him.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: And it's not just you. Nirvana Port, even EDGE... they're all colluding with you. The metropoles would love an excuse to finally discipline those unruly scientists.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: So, wouldn't it be simpler if you just kept me here? Unless the "just" guerrillas prefer to silence a little girl.
She knew she had the upper hand. A triumphant smile on her lips, she skipped cheerfully around the tent, the tense atmosphere only fueling her glee.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Home is so dreadfully boring. My family sells weapons everywhere but never sees a real battlefield. It's all mansions, deals, and counting money.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I'm sick of balls and banquets. Even hunting is just putting on airs. Soon enough, they'll just marry me off for some political alliance.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: So I snuck out. I'm going to have some fun before all that happens. And if I manage to pull off something big, my family will have to start listening to me.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I want to see real commanders! The powerful weapons from my books that can turn the tide of battle! And a horse! I want to ride one on the battlefield, like a proper general in those portraits!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...Your city-state is our enemy.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Arms dealers have no homeland, and the Andohars have no enemies. If you have the need and the money, my parents would be happy to do business. Complete confidentiality guaranteed.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Besides... are you sure you don't want to make use of me?
She looked at Dravyn, narrowing her eyes.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I've seen how you pick your weapons, buddy. You're that type—the kind who doesn't care how it gets done, or what it costs... as long as it works.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: You're hiding from the DisCity army, making backdoor deals with guerrillas... You must want something pretty badly. Something you'd do anything for.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: If you're bold enough to kill me, why not be bold enough to use me instead? Most of your soldiers can't do what I can. Even the metropoles haven't fully figured out my superpowers.
With a soft chuckle, the 11-year-old girl leaned forward, a hand clasped to her chest as she marketed herself eagerly as if possessed by a demon.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...This, right here, is a top-secret next-gen weapon. One that might flip a war on its head someday. Don't you want it? Don't you need it?

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Cut all that crap!
Before Dravyn could answer, someone else beat him to it. Brock grabbed the little girl by the back of her collar and hoisted her up into the air.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Aaaah—I'm so scared—ha!
Her magnetic power flared, launching a pen that stabbed clean through Brock's hand. But he didn't even flinch.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...? Take this!
A military knife flew through the air. He caught it between his teeth, then grabbed it with his free hand and stabbed it into the ground.
Catherine froze, her eyes darting toward a handgun nearby.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Save your energy, it's not even loaded. Look, I know your playbook: three-meter range, can't reshape objects, and the acceleration you generate is mediocre at best. Honestly, it's barely better than that superboy's tricks on TV.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: You're not stronger than me, kiddo. Don't underestimate the guerrillas. We're the reason your shiny home and all those metropoles are gonna come crashing down.
Catherine dangled in his grip, staring intently at Brock.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...With those? Your rusted-out guns and broken artillery? Please. You know that's not nearly enough.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Fine, if I can't join you... I could be a hostage! Why not just get some weapons from my family? It's just business—very good business for you. And since they'd still want me back, I'm sure I could get you a discount.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: You still don't get it.
With a sigh, he set the little girl down on a chair.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Look, kiddo, I might not be a dad, but my brother just got married. He and his wife are already picking out names for their three future kids. I get it. I know what parents are supposed to be.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Their whole job is to ensure their kid a happy life.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: The Andohars do want to make me happy. They make a lot of money to ensure it. And they are very serious about arranging my marriage.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: I don't give a damn about their money or their deals. That's not happiness. They've failed at what parents should do. Completely.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: You've never seen a real battlefield. You've never watched how fast a life can just... vanish. Out there, it doesn't matter that you're just a kid.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: The violence... it consumes everyone. Even the ones with a good heart.
Deep in thought, she listened attentively and then tilted her head to one side.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Then take me to see it?

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: No. I won't let you witness that. No child should.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: You should learn about the weight of life through love, not through hate and death. If your family didn't teach you that... then they don't deserve to be parents.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...So... you're still sending me away?
At this, Brock's cool-guy act crumbled. He scratched his head with a conflicted expression.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: I'm not that naive, kid. You've heard too much, and you've got all these dangerous ideas in your head. I can't risk the safety of my people.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: I'm sending you someplace where they can actually teach you what matters.
He picked up the phone.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Hey, it's me. Yeah, I need a favor. Again. I've got a... a situation. A little girl needs a place to— No no no, it's not like that! Just listen for a sec!! Your place is safe, right? I need somewhere trustworthy.
After a frantic scramble of explanations, the guerrilla leader hung up the phone, drenched in sweat.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: For now, I'll send you to Nirvana Port. Someone there will look after you, and you'll be safe and well-fed.
Dravyn stood speechless, and Catherine's face fell in disappointment.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...Fine. Last deal. You agree, and I promise I won't spill any of your little secrets.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Do you have horses in DisCity? The real, four-legged kind. Can I ride a horse to Nirvana Port? Come on, say yes! It'd be so cool if I got to ride one!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Just send her away! Right now!
After all the commotion, they finally picked a day without sandstorms and sent Catherine off on a small vehicle bound for Nirvana Port.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Relax, kiddo. We smashed them good last time. Took their spirit and their gear. They won't be dumb enough to come back for seconds. Who wants to bite off more than they can chew?

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: So enjoy the quiet while it lasts! Take a real breath for once.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: "Quiet"?
She turned back.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: It was a major victory, I'll give you that. But if I were running your operation... I'd be more careful now, not less.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Why would anyone go out of their way to crush an ant? They only would... if the ant showed it was strong enough to be a threat.
